label: late original-phase input j (diffuse late-input unit)
explanation: Sparse (about 1% of steps), diffuse unit. 80% of mass is in the original phase, rising with position (rate 0.4% at orig_idx 1 to 10% at orig_idx 8) and with L (longest sequences carry most mass); never fires at t=0 and almost never at <DEL>. The strongest single driver is input j (11.5x lift, 42% of mass), and the top activations are nearly all j at the last original positions; digits 2/0 and c, h also contribute, and prev_tok 0 boosts it. About 20% of mass sits in the first copy steps (recall_idx 1-2). The best simple predicate, j input at original position >= 4, gets only dev F1 0.32 / mass recall 0.35; adding token disjunctions (c, h, digits at late positions) reaches F1 0.34 / mass recall 0.55 at the cost of coherence. Not explained: much activation is spread across many tokens at late input positions and early copy steps, and j at early or mid positions is often inactive.
